summary:
Research handoff folding the second snapshot scenario into the map and recording the sourced reachability condition for that finding; preflight-validated with valid=True and no diagnostics.

What is recorded. The snapshot alignment finding now has two violated scenarios and a measured operational consequence: the first (execution 3d53c8e2) showed the install retains and reports an unconfirmed tail; the second (execution b9d811ad) showed the sharper effect — because the retained tail keeps the anchor index from being the effective last entry, the AppendEntries the leader sends after a successful install (anchored at the snapshot index) was rejected (append_success false) and the tail was left unchanged, so the very request that was supposed to truncate the tail could not. The branch note is added to b-install-snapshot-align and the fact f-log-snapshot-agreement keeps the mechanism.

New refinement from source: reachability with the default configuration is now characterised rather than left vague — installSnapshot's compaction is skipped entirely when the receiver's log end is at or below TrailingLogs, and when it runs the bound is min(snapshot index, log end − TrailingLogs), so the anchor is deleted while a tail survives only if the snapshot index sits at least TrailingLogs below the receiver's log end. Whether a real leader drives a follower into that shape, and how long the rejection lasts before the leader's nextIndex walk or another snapshot changes it, remain unmeasured.

Map change (base version 16): one branch note plus the narrowed Fact unknown; no trigger, guard, write, edge, requirement or previously accepted Surface changed, so the five violated scenarios, the two corroborating scenarios and all accepted results keep their original basis.

Run state: four confirmed in-scope violations (batching-FSM ConfigurationStore delivery, heartbeat fast-path header gate, TimeoutNow sender attribution, snapshot install log-tail alignment) with measured consequences for three of them, correspondence no_issue_found on every scenario, and no pending review work. Open frontier: the deployment reachability premises above; the two heartbeat/TimeoutNow reachability premises; whether batching FSMs are exempt from ConfigurationStore; the ReloadConfig, processHeartbeat-concurrency and transport TimeoutScale leads; and the still-unread in-memory snapshot store.
